question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An animal that has four feet.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Quadruped.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Quadruped" means an animal that has four feet, from the Latin “quattuor” (four) and “pes” (foot). (चार पैरों वाला जानवर)
◦ Example: A horse is a quadruped.

 

• The prefix "Quadru-/Quadri-" always denotes four, as seen in words like quadrilateral, quadrennial, and quadruplet.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Biped (द्विपाद प्राणी): An animal that has two feet, from Latin “bi” (two) and “pes” (foot).

 

• Option 3: Mammal (स्तनपायी): A warm-blooded animal that nurses its young with milk, from Latin “mamma” (breast).

 

• Option 4: Amphibian (उभयचर): An animal that can live both on land and in water, from Greek “amphi” (both) and “bios” (life).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "Quadri-/Quadru-" words frequently asked in SSC: Quadrilateral (a four-sided figure), Quadrennial (occurring every four years), Quadruplet (one of four children born at the same birth), Quadrangle (a four-sided courtyard), Quadricentennial (a four-hundredth anniversary) and Quadrivium (the four subjects of medieval study).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sybarite (भोग-विलासी): A person devoted to luxury and pleasure

2. Philanthropist (परोपकारी): A person who promotes the welfare of others

3. Xenophobia (विदेशियों का भय): Fear or hatred of foreigners or strangers

4. Astronaut (अंतरिक्ष यात्री): A person trained to travel in a spacecraft

5. Zoologist (प्राणि-विज्ञानी): A person who studies animals

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The art or science of drawing maps and charts.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Cartography.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Cartography" means the art or science of drawing maps and charts, from the Greek “khartes” (map/papyrus) and “graphein” (to write/draw). (मानचित्र बनाने की कला)
◦ Example: Modern cartography relies heavily on satellite imagery.

 

• The suffix "-graphy" always denotes the art, science, or process of writing or recording something, and the first part of the word tells us what is being recorded.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Topography (स्थलाकृति): The detailed description or study of the physical features of an area, from Greek “topos” (place).

 

• Option 3: Choreography (नृत्य रचना): The art of designing sequences of steps for dance, from Greek “khoreia” (dance).

 

• Option 4: Calligraphy (सुलेख): The art of beautiful and decorative handwriting, from Greek “kallos” (beauty).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-graphy" words frequently asked in SSC: Photography (capturing images using light), Biography (an account of someone's life), Autobiography (an account of one's own life written by oneself), Geography (the study of the earth's physical features), Typography (the art of arranging printed text) and Stenography (the art of shorthand writing).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Bibliophile (पुस्तक-प्रेमी): A person who loves or collects books

2. Claustrophobia (बंद स्थानों का भय): Fear of confined or enclosed spaces

3. Nostalgia (अतीत की याद): A sentimental longing for the past

4. Vagabond (आवारा): A person who wanders from place to place without a home

5. Numismatist (मुद्रा-शास्त्री): A person who collects or studies coins

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A group of ships, especially warships, sailing together under one command.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fleet.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Fleet" means a group of ships, especially warships, sailing together under one command. (जहाजों का बेड़ा)
◦ Example: The naval fleet set sail for the exercise at dawn.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Herd (पशुओं का झुंड): A large group of animals, especially cattle or wild animals, that live, feed, or migrate together.

 

• Option 2: Flock (पक्षियों/भेड़ों का झुंड): A group of birds, sheep, or goats seen or herded together.

 

• Option 4: Swarm (कीड़ों का झुंड): A large group of insects, especially bees, flying or moving together.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Fleet" frequently asked in SSC: Armada (a fleet of warships), Flotilla (a small fleet of ships or boats), Convoy (a group of vehicles or ships travelling together, often escorted), Squadron (a unit of warships or aircraft) and Navy (the entire sea-going military force of a nation).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Philatelist (डाक टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects postage stamps

2. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in seclusion, avoiding others

3. Epicure (स्वाद-प्रिय व्यक्ति): A person with refined taste in food and wine

4. Maverick (स्वतंत्र विचारक): A person who thinks and acts independently

5. Zealot (कट्टर समर्थक): A person fanatically committed to a cause

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A literary device or occurrence in which the actual outcome is the opposite of what was expected.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Situational irony.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Situational irony" means a literary or real-life occurrence in which the actual outcome of events is the opposite of what was expected, with “irony” itself deriving from the Greek “eironeia” (feigned ignorance). (जब जो होने की उम्मीद हो, उसके विपरीत घटित हो)
◦ Example: It was situational irony that the fire station burned to the ground.

 

• The various forms of "irony" are frequently tested together: dramatic irony involves the audience knowing more than the characters, verbal irony involves saying the opposite of what is meant, and situational irony involves outcomes that defy expectation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Verbal irony (वाचिक विडंबना): A figure of speech in which what is said is the opposite of what is actually meant.

 

• Option 2: Dramatic irony (नाटकीय विडंबना): A situation in which the audience knows something important that the characters in the story do not.

 

• Option 3: Paradox (विरोधाभास): A statement that seems self-contradictory or absurd but may nonetheless be true, from Greek “para” (contrary to) and “doxa” (opinion).

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Situational irony" frequently asked in SSC: Sarcasm (a sharp, often ironical remark meant to wound), Satire (using humour or ridicule to expose folly), Paradox (a self-contradictory but possibly true statement), Oxymoron (a figure of speech combining contradictory terms) and Anticlimax (a disappointing end to something that had built up expectation).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others to gain favour

2. Charlatan (ढोंगी): A person falsely claiming expert knowledge

3. Pedant (क्षुद्र नियमवादी): A person overly concerned with minor rules or details

4. Chauvinist (पक्षपाती/अंधराष्ट्रवादी): A person with excessive or biased devotion to a cause

5. Cynic (निंदक): A person who distrusts human sincerity and motives

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who practises strict self-denial and abstains from worldly pleasures for spiritual discipline.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Ascetic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Ascetic" means a person who practises strict self-denial and abstains from worldly pleasures as a form of spiritual discipline, from the Greek “askesis” (exercise/training). (तपस्वी)
◦ Example: The ascetic renounced all his wealth to live in the forest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Hedonist (सुखवादी): A person who believes the pursuit of pleasure is the most important goal in life, from Greek “hedone” (pleasure).

 

• Option 3: Epicurean (विलासप्रिय व्यक्ति): A person devoted to refined and luxurious sensory enjoyment, named after the philosopher Epicurus.

 

• Option 4: Puritan (कट्टर नैतिकतावादी): A person with strict moral or religious views, especially one opposed to self-indulgence and luxury.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Ascetic" frequently asked in SSC: Hermit (a person living in solitude for religious reasons), Recluse (a person who avoids the company of others), Puritan (a person with strict moral views), Stoic (a person who endures hardship without complaint), Fakir (a Muslim or Hindu religious ascetic) and Anchorite (a person who lives in religious seclusion).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Plagiarist (साहित्यिक चोर): A person who copies another's work and passes it off as their own

2. Truant (विद्यालय से अनुपस्थित रहने वाला): A student who stays away from school without permission

3. Vagrant (आवारा/बेघर): A person without a settled home or livelihood

4. Malingerer (बहानेबाज): A person who pretends to be ill to avoid work

5. Prodigy (अद्भुत प्रतिभाशाली बालक): A person, especially a child, with exceptional talent

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The philosophical system holding that human knowledge is shaped and limited by the structures of the mind itself.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Kantianism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Kantianism" means the philosophical system of Immanuel Kant, which holds that human knowledge is shaped and limited by the innate structures of the mind rather than being a direct copy of reality. (कांट का दर्शन, जिसके अनुसार ज्ञान मानव मस्तिष्क की सीमाओं द्वारा निर्धारित होता है)
◦ Example: Her thesis examined Kantianism and its influence on modern ethics.

 

• The suffix "-ism" often denotes a distinctive doctrine, theory, or system of belief, frequently attached to a philosopher's name (e.g., Kantianism, Marxism, Platonism) or to a guiding principle (e.g., Rationalism, Empiricism).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Empiricism (अनुभववाद): The theory that all knowledge is derived primarily from sensory experience, from Greek “empeiria” (experience).

 

• Option 3: Rationalism (बुद्धिवाद): The theory that reason, rather than experience, is the chief source and test of knowledge, from Latin “ratio” (reason).

 

• Option 4: Utilitarianism (उपयोगितावाद): The ethical theory that the right action is the one producing the greatest happiness for the greatest number.

 

NOTE

 

• Other philosophical "-ism" terms frequently asked in SSC: Stoicism (enduring hardship without complaint), Existentialism (emphasis on individual freedom and choice), Platonism (belief in ideal, non-material forms), Marxism (the theory of class struggle and economic history), Pragmatism (judging ideas by their practical consequences) and Nihilism (the belief that life is without objective meaning).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ambidextrous (दोनों हाथों से समान रूप से काम करने वाला): Able to use both hands equally well

2. Novice (नौसिखिया): A person new to or inexperienced in a field

3. Virtuoso (निपुण कलाकार): A person highly skilled in an art, especially music

4. Connoisseur (पारखी): A person with expert knowledge and taste in a field

5. Dilettante (छिछला रुचि रखने वाला): A person with a superficial interest in an art or field

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An abnormal fear of open, crowded, or public spaces.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Agoraphobia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Agoraphobia" means an abnormal fear of open, crowded, or public spaces from which escape might be difficult, from the Greek “agora” (marketplace) and “phobos” (fear). (खुले या भीड़ भरे सार्वजनिक स्थानों का भय)
◦ Example: Her agoraphobia made it difficult for her to travel on crowded trains.

 

• The suffix "-phobia" always denotes an irrational or excessive fear, and the first part of the word tells us what is feared.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Claustrophobia (बंद स्थानों का भय): An abnormal fear of confined or enclosed spaces, from Latin “claustrum” (a closed place).

 

• Option 2: Acrophobia (ऊँचाई का भय): An abnormal fear of heights, from Greek “akron” (summit/peak).

 

• Option 4: Xenophobia (विदेशियों का भय): An intense dislike or fear of strangers or foreigners, from Greek “xenos” (stranger).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-phobia" words frequently asked in SSC: Hydrophobia (fear of water), Photophobia (fear/intolerance of light), Nyctophobia (fear of the dark), Pyrophobia (fear of fire), Arachnophobia (fear of spiders) and Zoophobia (fear of animals).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Anarchy (अराजकता): Absence of government or law and order

2. Autocracy (एकतंत्र): Government by a single ruler with absolute power

3. Aeronaut (वैमानिक): A person who operates or travels in a balloon or airship

4. Kleptomaniac (चोरी की सनक वाला व्यक्ति): A person with an irresistible urge to steal

5. Etymologist (व्युत्पत्ति-शास्त्री): A person who studies the origin of words

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who dislikes or distrusts humankind in general.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Misanthrope.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Misanthrope" means a person who dislikes or distrusts humankind in general, from the Greek “misein” (to hate) and “anthropos” (human being). (मनुष्य-द्वेषी)
◦ Example: After years of betrayal, he became a bitter misanthrope who avoided all company.

 

• The prefix "Mis-" always denotes hatred or dislike, and the rest of the word tells us who or what is hated (e.g., gyne = woman, andros = man, gamos = marriage, anthropos = mankind).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Misogynist (स्त्री-द्वेषी): A person who dislikes, despises, or is deeply prejudiced against women, from Greek “gyne” (woman).

 

• Option 2: Misogamist (विवाह-द्वेषी): A person who hates or opposes marriage, from Greek “gamos” (marriage).

 

• Option 3: Misandrist (पुरुष-द्वेषी): A person who dislikes, despises, or is deeply prejudiced against men, from Greek “andros” (man).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "Mis-" words frequently asked in SSC: Misogamist (hates marriage), Misogynist (hates women), Misandrist (hates men), Misocapnist (hates smoking), Misoneist (hates change or novelty) and Misology (hatred of reasoning or argument).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Arsonist (आगजनी करने वाला): A person who deliberately sets fire to property

2. Assassin (गुप्त हत्यारा): A person who murders an important person for political or religious reasons

3. Genocide (जनसंहार): The deliberate killing of a large group from a particular nation or ethnicity

4. Perjurer (झूठी गवाही देने वाला): A person who lies under oath

5. Embezzler (गबन करने वाला): A person who steals money entrusted to their care

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who pretends to have moral beliefs, principles, or virtues that they do not actually possess.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Hypocrite.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Hypocrite" means a person who pretends to have moral beliefs, principles, or virtues that they do not actually possess, from the Greek “hypokrites” (an actor, a pretender). (पाखंडी/कपटी)
◦ Example: He was called a hypocrite for preaching honesty while cheating on his taxes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Charlatan (ढोंगी विशेषज्ञ): A person who falsely claims to have expert knowledge or skill, especially in medicine.

 

• Option 3: Impostor (धोखेबाज़/प्रतिरूपक): A person who pretends to be someone else in order to deceive others.

 

• Option 4: Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others excessively in order to gain personal advantage.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Hypocrite" frequently asked in SSC: Charlatan (a fraudulent expert), Impostor (one who deceives by pretending to be someone else), Sycophant (a flatterer for self-interest), Pharisee (a self-righteous, hypocritical person) and Dissembler (one who conceals true feelings or intentions).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Herbivore (शाकाहारी प्राणी): An animal that feeds only on plants

2. Carnivore (मांसाहारी प्राणी): An animal that feeds on flesh

3. Omnivore (सर्वाहारी प्राणी): An animal that eats both plants and meat

4. Cannibal (नरभक्षी): A person or animal that eats the flesh of its own kind

5. Nomad (खानाबदोश): A person who moves from place to place without a permanent home

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A dramatic and suspenseful situation, especially at the end of an episode or chapter, that leaves the audience eager for what happens next.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Cliffhanger.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Cliffhanger" means a dramatic and suspenseful situation, especially at the end of an episode or chapter, that leaves the audience eager for what happens next. (तनावपूर्ण/रोमांचक मोड़, जो उत्सुकता बनाए रखे)
◦ Example: The season finale ended on a cliffhanger that left fans guessing for months.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Denouement (कथा का समापन): The final part of a story in which the strands of the plot are drawn together and resolved, from French “denouer” (to untie).

 

• Option 3: Climax (चरम बिंदु): The point of greatest intensity or a decisive turning point in a narrative, from Greek “klimax” (ladder).

 

• Option 4: Anticlimax (अवरोही अंत): A disappointing or trivial conclusion to something that had built up great expectations.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Cliffhanger" frequently asked in SSC: Denouement (the final resolution of a plot), Climax (the point of highest tension), Anticlimax (a letdown after rising expectation), Suspense (a state of anxious uncertainty) and Foreshadowing (a hint of events yet to come).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Regicide (राजहत्या): The killing of a king

2. Deicide (ईश्वर-हत्या): The killing of a god

3. Herbicide (खरपतवारनाशी): A substance used to destroy unwanted plants

4. Bureaucracy (नौकरशाही): Government administered mainly by government officials

5. Theocracy (धर्मतंत्र): Government ruled by religious authority

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who attacks, criticizes, or seeks to overthrow cherished beliefs or traditional institutions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Iconoclast.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Iconoclast" means a person who attacks, criticizes, or seeks to overthrow cherished beliefs or traditional institutions, from the Greek “eikon” (image) and “klastes” (breaker). (परंपरा या मान्यताओं पर प्रहार करने वाला व्यक्ति)
◦ Example: The young artist was seen as an iconoclast who rejected every convention of classical painting.

 

• The suffix "-clast" always denotes a breaker or destroyer, as in iconoclast (breaker of images/beliefs) and osteoclast (a cell that breaks down bone tissue).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Conformist (अनुरूपतावादी): A person who conforms to accepted behaviour or generally held views.

 

• Option 2: Traditionalist (परंपरावादी): A person who values and adheres to long-established customs and beliefs.

 

• Option 4: Loyalist (निष्ठावान): A person who remains strongly loyal to an established ruler, government, or cause.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Iconoclast" frequently asked in SSC: Rebel (one who resists authority), Nonconformist (one who does not follow accepted conventions), Maverick (an independent-minded person), Heretic (one who holds beliefs contrary to established doctrine) and Radical (one who advocates thorough reform).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Forger (जालसाज़): A person who produces fake documents or currency

2. Fugitive (फरार व्यक्ति): A person fleeing from justice or danger

3. Mercenary (भाड़े का सैनिक): A professional soldier hired to serve a foreign army

4. Utopia (काल्पनिक आदर्श स्थान): An imagined place or state in which everything is perfect

5. Dystopia (डरावनी काल्पनिक दुनिया): An imagined state in which there is great suffering or injustice

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An award, honour, or expression of praise given in recognition of an achievement.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Accolade.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Accolade" means an award, honour, or expression of praise given in recognition of an achievement, from the Latin “ad” (to) and “collum” (neck) — originally referring to an embrace or a touch on the shoulder used to confer knighthood. (सम्मान/पुरस्कार)
◦ Example: Winning the national award was the greatest accolade of her career.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Reprimand (डांट/भर्त्सना): A formal or official statement of disapproval or rebuke, from Latin “reprimere” (to check/repress).

 

• Option 2: Stigma (कलंक): A mark of disgrace or shame associated with a particular circumstance or quality, from Greek “stigma” (a mark made by a pointed instrument).

 

• Option 3: Eulogy (प्रशस्ति भाषण): A speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly, especially a tribute to someone who has died, from Greek “eu” (well) and “logos” (word/speech).

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Accolade" frequently asked in SSC: Tribute (an act or statement expressing admiration or respect), Laurel (an honour or distinction won for achievement), Citation (a formal mention of praiseworthy conduct), Commendation (formal praise or approval) and Homage (a public expression of respect or honour).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Martinet (कठोर अनुशासनप्रिय व्यक्ति): A strict disciplinarian who insists on rigid adherence to rules

2. Bibliomaniac (पुस्तकों का सनकी शौकीन): A person with an extreme, obsessive love of books

3. Choreographer (नृत्य रचनाकार): A person who designs sequences of steps for dance

4. Genealogist (वंशावली विशेषज्ञ): A person who studies family history and lineage

5. Entomologist (कीट-विज्ञानी): A person who studies insects

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A short, witty, and often paradoxical saying or short poem.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Epigram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Epigram" means a short, witty, and often paradoxical saying or short poem, from the Greek “epi” (upon) and “gramma” (something written). (सूक्ति/चुटीला कथन)
◦ Example: Oscar Wilde was famous for his clever epigrams.

 

• The prefix "Epi-" often means upon, in addition to, or after, and appears in related literary terms such as epitaph (writing upon a tomb), epilogue (words after the main text), and epithet (a word placed upon/alongside a name).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Epitaph (समाधि-लेख): An inscription on a tombstone or a short statement commemorating a dead person, from Greek “epi” (upon) and “taphos” (tomb).

 

• Option 3: Epilogue (उपसंहार): A short section at the end of a literary work that comments on or concludes it, from Greek “epi” (upon/after) and “logos” (speech).

 

• Option 4: Epithet (उपनाम/विशेषण): A descriptive word or phrase expressing a quality regarded as characteristic of a person or thing, from Greek “epitheton” (added, attributed).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "Epi-" words frequently asked in SSC: Epitaph (an inscription on a tomb), Epilogue (a concluding section of a book), Epithet (a descriptive nickname), Epicentre (the point directly above an earthquake's origin), Epidemic (a widespread outbreak of disease) and Epidermis (the outer layer of the skin).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Astrologer (ज्योतिषी): A person who studies the influence of celestial bodies on human affairs

2. Astronomer (खगोलशास्त्री): A person who studies celestial objects and phenomena scientifically

3. Calligrapher (सुलेखक): A person skilled in decorative handwriting

4. Plutocracy (धनिकतंत्र): Government controlled by the wealthy

5. Meritocracy (योग्यतातंत्र): A system in which power is held by those with the most ability

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An abnormal fear of clustered patterns of small holes or bumps.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Trypophobia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Trypophobia" means an abnormal fear of clusters of small holes or bumps, from the Greek “trypa” (hole) and “phobos” (fear). (छिद्रों या गुच्छों का भय)
◦ Example: Looking at the honeycomb pattern triggered her trypophobia.

 

• The suffix "-phobia" always denotes an irrational fear, and the first part of the word tells us what is feared.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Nyctophobia (अंधेरे का भय): An abnormal fear of darkness or night, from the Greek “nyx” (night).

 

• Option 3: Agoraphobia (खुले स्थानों का भय): An abnormal fear of open or crowded public spaces, from the Greek “agora” (marketplace).

 

• Option 4: Claustrophobia (बंद स्थानों का भय): An abnormal fear of confined or enclosed spaces, from the Latin “claustrum” (a closed space).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-phobia" words frequently asked in SSC: Acrophobia (heights), Xenophobia (strangers or foreigners), Nyctophobia (darkness), Agoraphobia (open or crowded spaces), Claustrophobia (confined spaces), Hydrophobia (water), Photophobia (light) and Arachnophobia (spiders).

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Based on logical reasoning rather than emotion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Rational.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Rational" means based on logical reasoning rather than emotion, from the Latin “ratio” (reason, calculation). (तर्कसंगत)
◦ Example: She made a rational decision after weighing all the facts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Impulsive (आवेगी): Acting or done without forethought, based on sudden feeling rather than reason.

 

• Option 2: Arbitrary (मनमाना): Based on random choice or personal whim rather than reason or system.

 

• Option 4: Intuitive (सहज ज्ञान से युक्त): Based on instinct or feeling rather than conscious reasoning.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Rational" frequently asked in SSC: Logical (based on sound reasoning), Sensible (having good judgement), Judicious (having or showing good sense), Pragmatic (dealing with things sensibly and practically) and Reasonable (fair and sensible).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Philanthropist (परोपकारी): A person who seeks to promote the welfare of others

2. Vagabond (आवारा): A person who wanders without a settled home

3. Connoisseur (पारखी): An expert judge in matters of art or taste

4. Pragmatist (व्यवहारवादी): A person who deals with things practically

5. Iconoclast (रूढ़िभंजक): A person who attacks established beliefs or institutions

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Mysterious and difficult to interpret or understand.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Enigmatic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Enigmatic" means mysterious and difficult to interpret or understand, from the Greek “ainigma” (riddle). (रहस्यमय)
◦ Example: The old man gave an enigmatic smile and said nothing more.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Lucid (सुस्पष्ट): Expressed clearly and easy to understand, from the Latin “lucidus” (clear, bright).

 

• Option 2: Explicit (स्पष्ट): Stated clearly and in detail, leaving nothing implied.

 

• Option 3: Transparent (पारदर्शी): Easy to perceive or understand; obvious and without disguise.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Enigmatic" frequently asked in SSC: Cryptic (having a hidden meaning), Abstruse (difficult to understand), Esoteric (understood by only a small group), Ambiguous (open to more than one interpretation) and Inscrutable (impossible to interpret or understand).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters others for personal gain

2. Neophyte (नौसिखिया): A person who is new to a subject or activity

3. Gourmand (पेटू): A person who loves eating and drinking, sometimes excessively

4. Zealot (कट्टरपंथी): A person who is fanatical about a cause

5. Charlatan (ढोंगी): A person falsely claiming to have expert knowledge

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Meticulous.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Meticulous" means showing great attention to detail and extreme care, from the Latin “meticulosus” (fearful), itself from “metus” (fear). (अत्यंत सावधान)
◦ Example: The auditor was meticulous in checking every entry in the ledger.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Cursory (सरसरी): Done quickly and without attention to detail; hasty and superficial.

 

• Option 3: Careless (लापरवाह): Not giving sufficient attention or thought to avoiding harm or errors.

 

• Option 4: Haphazard (अव्यवस्थित): Lacking any obvious organization or plan; done randomly.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Meticulous" frequently asked in SSC: Punctilious (showing great attention to detail), Fastidious (very attentive to detail and hard to please), Scrupulous (diligent and thorough), Painstaking (done with great care) and Assiduous (showing great care and perseverance).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Hedonist (सुखवादी): A person who believes pleasure is the most important thing in life

2. Pacifist (शांतिवादी): A person who believes in the peaceful resolution of disputes

3. Plagiarist (साहित्यिक चोर): A person who copies another's work and claims it as their own

4. Ascetic (तपस्वी): A person who practises severe self-discipline for spiritual reasons

5. Mercenary (भाड़े का सैनिक): A soldier who fights for payment rather than loyalty

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who loves work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Ergophile.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Ergophile" means a person who loves work, from the Greek “ergon” (work) and “philos” (loving). (काम से प्रेम करने वाला)
◦ Example: A true ergophile, he volunteered for extra shifts even during the holidays.

 

• The suffix "-phile" always denotes a lover or enthusiast of something, and the first part of the word tells us what is loved.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Technophile (तकनीक प्रेमी): A person who is enthusiastic about new technology, from the Greek “tekhne” (art, skill).

 

• Option 3: Xenophile (विदेशी संस्कृति प्रेमी): A person attracted to foreign peoples, cultures, or customs, from the Greek “xenos” (stranger).

 

• Option 4: Cynophile (कुत्ता प्रेमी): A person who loves or is fond of dogs, from the Greek “kyon” (dog).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-phile" words frequently asked in SSC: Bibliophile (books), Ailurophile (cats), Cynophile (dogs), Anglophile (English culture), Technophile (technology), Xenophile (foreign cultures) and Audiophile (high-quality sound reproduction).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Martinet (कठोर अनुशासक): A person who demands strict adherence to rules

2. Renegade (विद्रोही): A person who deserts a cause or group

3. Prodigal (अपव्ययी): A person who is wastefully extravagant

4. Maverick (स्वतंत्र विचारों वाला व्यक्ति): An independent-minded person who does not follow the crowd

5. Dilettante (शौकिया कलाप्रेमी): A person with only a superficial interest in an art or field

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The science or art of cultivating fruits, vegetables, and flowers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Horticulture.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Horticulture" means the science or art of cultivating fruits, vegetables, and flowers, from the Latin “hortus” (garden) and “cultura” (cultivation). (बागवानी)
◦ Example: The state government set up a horticulture department to promote fruit farming.

 

• The suffix "-culture" always denotes the cultivation or rearing of something, and the first part of the word tells us what is cultivated or reared.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Sericulture (रेशम कीट पालन): The rearing of silkworms for the commercial production of silk, from the Greek “serikos” (silken).

 

• Option 2: Apiculture (मधुमक्खी पालन): The practice of keeping bees, chiefly for honey, from the Latin “apis” (bee).

 

• Option 4: Agriculture (कृषि): The broad science and practice of cultivating land, raising crops, and rearing livestock.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-culture" words frequently asked in SSC: Sericulture (silkworms), Apiculture (bees), Pisciculture (fish), Viticulture (grapes/vines), Floriculture (flowers), Silviculture (forest trees) and Aquaculture (aquatic organisms).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Bigamist (द्विविवाही): A person who marries while already married to another

2. Vandal (विध्वंसक): A person who deliberately destroys or damages property

3. Interloper (अनधिकार हस्तक्षेप करने वाला): A person who interferes in others' affairs without invitation

5. Chauvinist (अंधराष्ट्रवादी): A person with excessive, biased devotion to their own group

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Incapable of being wrong or making a mistake.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Infallible.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Infallible" means incapable of being wrong or making a mistake, from the Latin “in-” (not) and “fallere” (to deceive). (अचूक)
◦ Example: No system is truly infallible, however well designed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Fallible (भ्रमशील): Capable of making mistakes or being wrong, the direct opposite of infallible.

 

• Option 2: Erroneous (त्रुटिपूर्ण): Containing errors or being incorrect in fact or judgement.

 

• Option 3: Precarious (अनिश्चित): Not securely held or in position; dangerously likely to fail.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Infallible" frequently asked in SSC: Impeccable (faultless, flawless), Unerring (always right or accurate), Foolproof (incapable of going wrong), Flawless (without any imperfections) and Unimpeachable (not able to be doubted or questioned).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Insomniac (अनिद्रा रोगी): A person who habitually finds it difficult to sleep

2. Kleptomaniac (चोरी की सनक वाला): A person with an uncontrollable urge to steal

3. Vegan (शुद्ध शाकाहारी): A person who eats no food derived from animals

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A post-mortem examination of a dead body to determine the cause of death.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Autopsy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Autopsy" means a post-mortem examination of a dead body to determine the cause of death, from the Greek “autos” (self) and “opsis” (seeing) — literally “to see for oneself”. (शव परीक्षा)
◦ Example: The autopsy revealed that the victim had been poisoned.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Biopsy (जीवित ऊतक परीक्षण): The examination of tissue removed from a living body to diagnose disease.

 

• Option 3: Dissection (विच्छेदन): The action of cutting up a body, plant, or animal to study its internal structure.

 

• Option 4: Exhumation (कब्र से शव निकालना): The act of digging up a body that has been buried, especially for examination.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Autopsy" frequently asked in SSC: Post-mortem (examination after death), Necropsy (examination of an animal's body after death), Biopsy (examination of living tissue), Dissection (cutting up for study) and Exhumation (digging up a buried body).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Cosmopolitan (विश्वबंधु): A person who feels at home in every country

2. Egoist (अहंवादी): A person who thinks only of themselves

3. Optimist (आशावादी): A person who always expects a favourable outcome

4. Herbivore (शाकाहारी प्राणी): An animal that feeds only on plants

5. Polyglot (बहुभाषाविद्): A person who knows and can use several languages

• Option 4: Cynophobia (कुत्तों का भय): An abnormal fear of dogs, from the Greek “kyon” (dog).

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who lives alone and deliberately avoids the company of others.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Recluse.

• "Recluse" means a person who lives alone and deliberately avoids the company of others, from the Late Latin “reclusus” (shut away, kept apart). (संन्यासी / समाज से दूर)

• Option 1: Extrovert (बहिर्मुखी): An outgoing, socially confident person who enjoys the company of others.

 

• Option 2: Socialite (समाज में लोकप्रिय व्यक्ति): A person who is prominent in fashionable society and frequently attends social events.

 

• Option 4: Introvert (अंतर्मुखी): A shy, reserved person who prefers solitary activities over large social gatherings.

• Other words close in meaning to "Recluse" frequently asked in SSC: Hermit (one who lives in solitude, often for religious reasons), Misanthrope (one who hates mankind), Loner (a person who prefers being alone), Anchorite (a religious recluse) and Solitary (a person who lives alone).

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A worker skilled in a particular craft, who makes things by hand.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Artisan.

• Option 2: Apprentice (प्रशिक्षु): A person learning a trade from a skilled employer, not yet fully trained.

 

• Option 3: Novice (नौसिखिया): A person new to, and inexperienced in, a field or activity.

5. Epicure (स्वादिष्ट भोजन का शौकीन): A person with refined tastes in food and wine

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Event horizon.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Event horizon" means the boundary around a black hole beyond which no matter or light can ever escape its gravitational pull. (घटना क्षितिज)
◦ Example: Once a spacecraft crosses the event horizon of a black hole, it can never return.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Singularity (विलक्षणता): The point at the centre of a black hole where gravity and density are believed to become infinite.

 

• Option 3: Nebula (निहारिका): A giant interstellar cloud of dust, hydrogen, and other gases, often the birthplace of stars.

 

• Option 4: Supernova (अतिनवतारा): A powerful and luminous explosion that occurs at the end of a massive star's life.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Event horizon" frequently asked in SSC: Singularity (the point of infinite density in a black hole), Black hole (a region of extremely strong gravity from which nothing escapes), Nebula (a cloud of gas and dust in space), Supernova (the explosive death of a star) and Wormhole (a hypothetical tunnel connecting distant points in space-time).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Xenophobe (विदेशियों से घृणा करने वाला): A person who fears or hates foreigners

2. Workaholic (काम का आदी): A person who compulsively works excessively hard

3. Somnambulist (नींद में चलने वाला): A person who walks about while asleep

4. Antiquarian (पुरावस्तु विशेषज्ञ): A person who studies or collects antiques

5. Pyromaniac (आग लगाने की सनक वाला): A person with an obsessive desire to set things on fire
